monthly_review.summary: You've increased volume and intensity this month, with faster average pace and higher aerobic training effect, but cadence dipped slightly and efficiency improved marginally.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite running 4 fewer sessions and 9.4 km less than last month, your average pace improved by 20 sec/km and aerobic TE rose by 0.3 — indicating higher-intensity distribution and better effort efficiency.

goal_tracker.message: You need 9.4 more km across 4 remaining sessions — averaging 2.35 km per session — to match last month's volume. Prioritize consistency: even three 3-km Zone 2 runs (e.g., 3 × 3.2 km) would cover the gap.

insights.title: Efficiency is trending upward
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency improved from 13.46 to 13.52 km/hr per bpm — a small but meaningful gain, especially given higher average HR (144 vs 140) and faster pace (519 vs 539 sec/km). This suggests better cardiovascular coupling at submaximal efforts.

insights.title: Zone 3–4 dominance increased significantly
insights.body: Time in Z3+Z4 rose from 46% (31% Z3 + 15% Z4) in June to 46% (27% Z3 + 19% Z4) in July — but crucially, Z5 jumped from 1% to 7%, indicating more frequent high-intensity efforts, likely contributing to the HR increase and pace improvement.

insights.title: Cadence-stride tradeoff evident in long runs
insights.body: During your 14.1 km run (7/12), cadence was 151 spm but stride length dropped to 70.36 cm and ground contact time rose to 319 ms — both outliers vs recent shorter runs (e.g., 86.42 cm stride, 312 ms GCT on 7/15). This signals form fatigue late in long efforts.

insights.title: Recovery may be compromised
insights.body: Five of your last five runs occurred within 9 days (7/6–7/17), with only one rest day between the 14.1 km (7/12) and next run (7/15). Average aerobic TE is now 3.1 over those five runs — above the sustainable ~2.8 threshold for recreational runners without built-in recovery runs.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a strict 5.0 km Zone 2 effort (HR ≤135 bpm), focusing on cadence ≥148 spm and minimizing vertical oscillation (<7.5 cm) — use your 7/08 run (129 bpm, 136 spm, 7.6 cm VO) as a baseline to improve form under low stress.
recommendations.reason: Your Zone 2 time dropped from 29% to 33% but avg HR in Zone 2 runs has crept up; this session rebuilds aerobic base while addressing cadence decline and VO drift.

recommendations.action: Insert a full rest day before your next long run — do not run within 72 hours of your 12.0 km effort on 7/17.
recommendations.reason: Consecutive high-TE runs (3.1–3.3) with <48h recovery risk cumulative fatigue, evidenced by rising ground contact time (300→319 ms) and falling stride length in long efforts.

recommendations.action: On your next medium run (6–8 km), perform 4 × 1-min strides at 475 sec/km pace (your best pace) with 90s walk recovery — monitor vertical oscillation and aim to hold it ≤7.5 cm (vs current 7.7–7.9 cm).
recommendations.reason: Your best pace (475 sec/km) is 44 sec/km faster than July avg — strides at this pace reinforce neuromuscular efficiency while targeting VO, which correlates strongly with running economy.

weekly_focus.description: Strengthen your ability to maintain efficient biomechanics across varying durations and intensities — especially as fatigue accumulates — while protecting recovery capacity.
suggested_sessions: Zone 2 Recovery Run (5 km, HR ≤135 bpm, cadence ≥148 spm)
Strides + Easy Run (6 km total, 4 × 1-min at 475 sec/km)
Long Run with Form Checkpoints (10 km, pause at km 3/6/9 to verify VO <7.6 cm and GCT <310 ms)
